title: Interpretability-by-Design with Accurate Locally Additive Models and Conditional Feature Effects
claim: A locally additive model keeps per-feature plots but lets effects vary by region, capturing interactions while remaining auditable.
layout: 4 panels in a row joined by plus signs, equation reading left-to-right
description: A horizontal equation-style figure: a bias term β0 (189) plus three per-feature plots, then an ellipsis labeled "8 more", equals ŷ (rentals/h). The first plot, hour, splits on working day: an orange working-day curve with commute-time peaks around 8 and 17, and a blue day-off curve that is smoother with a midday hump. A dotted vertical line near hour 6 and an up arrow mark where the other features' regions switch. The second plot, temperature, splits on hour: orange (hour ≥ 7) rises to a peak near 28°C, and blue (hour ≤ 6) stays nearly flat. The third plot, humidity, has a single blue step curve because it has no interaction. Orange and blue color-code the regions, and plus signs link the plots into a sum. The eye goes first to the colorful curves, then to the equation structure.
caption: A CALM fitted on the Bike Sharing dataset: the prediction sums one plot per feature, each plot holding one curve per region. The hour splits on the working day; the temperature splits on the hour, mattering by day and barely at night; the humidity interacts with no feature and keeps one curve. The dotted line on the hour's plot marks where the temperature's and the year's regions switch and its arrow gives the sign of the hidden jump; Section [ref] explains it in depth.
abstract: Generalized additive models (GAMs) offer high interpretability through independent univariate feature effects but underfit when interactions are present in data. GA$^2$Ms add selected pairwise interactions, which improves accuracy, but sacrifices interpretability. We propose Conditionally Additive Local Models (CALMs), a new model class that narrows this trade-off: it stays close to GAMs in interpretability and close to GA$^2$Ms in accuracy. CALMs allow multiple univariate shape functions per feature, each active in different regions of the input space. These regions are defined independently for each feature as simple logical conditions (thresholds) on the features it interacts with. As a result, effects remain locally additive while varying across subregions to capture interactions. We further propose a principled distillation-based training pipeline that identifies homogeneous regions with limited interactions and fits interpretable shape functions via region-aware backfitting. Experiments on diverse classification and regression tasks show that CALMs never underperform GAMs, often beat them and achieve accuracy broadly comparable to GA$^2$Ms, while preserving the univariate auditability that GA$^2$Ms forfeit.
